definitions.explanation: The middle point of a process or journey; neither the beginning nor the end.

examples.japanese: {中途|ちゅうと}で{諦|あきら}めてはいけない。
examples.english: You must not give up halfway.

examples.japanese: {中途|ちゅうと}{採用|さいよう}で{入社|にゅうしゃ}した。
examples.english: I joined the company through mid-career hiring.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}が{中途|ちゅうと}で{頓挫|とんざ}した。
{中途|ちゅうと}{半端|はんぱ}な{気持|きも}ちでは{何|なに}も{成功|せいこう}しない。
examples.english: You won't succeed at anything with a half-hearted attitude.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{中途|ちゅうと}{採用|さいよう}で{入社|にゅうしゃ}したが、{今|いま}では{部長|ぶちょう}にまで{昇進|しょうしん}している。
examples.english: He joined the company through mid-career hiring, but has now risen to department head.

notes:
{中途|ちゅうと} means midway or halfway through a process. It often carries a connotation of incompleteness or stopping before reaching the end.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {中途|ちゅうと}{半端|はんぱ}: half-finished, halfhearted, incomplete
- {中途|ちゅうと}{採用|さいよう}: mid-career hiring (as opposed to {新卒|しんそつ}{採用|さいよう})
- {中途|ちゅうと}{退学|たいがく}: dropping out of school
- {中途|ちゅうと}で{止|や}める: to quit halfway

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {途中|とちゅう}: on the way, midway (neutral, no negative connotation)
- {半|なか}ば: halfway, middle
- {中途|ちゅうと} typically implies something was left unfinished, while {途中|とちゅう} simply marks a point along the way

NOTE:
{中途|ちゅうと}{採用|さいよう} is an important business term in Japan, where most companies traditionally hire through {新卒|しんそつ}{一括|いっかつ}{採用|さいよう} (mass hiring of new graduates).
